report_name: Storm Ransomware Group Claims Attack on Canadian Hospital

threat_actors.name: Storm
threat_actors.description: A new but aggressive ransomware group that emerged in August 2026, known for its high operational tempo and use of AI-driven chat for victim communications. It operates a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model and employs double extortion tactics.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Used to steal sensitive data, including patient records and hospital operational data, before encrypting files as part of a double extortion strategy.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The ransomware payload was deployed to encrypt critical systems across the hospital's network, disrupting operations and demanding a ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The ransomware operators likely deleted volume shadow copies to prevent recovery from local backups, a common tactic for ransomware groups.

attack_patterns.name: Service Execution
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely used legitimate tools like PsExec for lateral movement and to deploy their ransomware payload across the hospital network.

malware.name: Storm Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload deployed by the Storm group to encrypt critical systems and exfiltrate data as part of their double extortion attacks against organizations like the Nipigon District Memorial Hospital.

tools.name: PsExec
tools.description: A legitimate remote administration tool likely used by the Storm group for lateral movement and to deploy their ransomware payload.

tools.name: wmic
tools.description: The Windows Management Instrumentation Command-line utility, likely used by the Storm group for lateral movement and remote execution of their ransomware.

identities.name: Nipigon District Memorial Hospital
identities.description: A hospital in Ontario, Canada, that suffered a ransomware attack by the Storm group, identified on October 4, 2026.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b8a1c9e-5d3f-4e7b-8a1c-9e5d3f4e7b8a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common precursor to ransomware attacks.
references:
  - https://www.hookphish.com/blog/ransomware-group-storm-hits-nipigon-district-memorial-hospital/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-05
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the command used to delete volume shadow copies, a technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.

indicators.name: PsExec or WMIC for Remote Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: PsExec or WMIC for Remote Execution
id: 9e5d3f4e-7b8a-4c1d-8a1c-2b8a1c9e5d3f
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of PsExec or WMIC, which are frequently used by ransomware groups for lateral movement and remote execution of payloads.
references:
  - https://www.hookphish.com/blog/ransomware-group-storm-hits-nipigon-district-memorial-hospital/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-05
tags:
  - attack.t1569.002
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\PsExec.exe'
      - '\Psexesvc.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of PsExec or WMIC, tools commonly used by ransomware actors for lateral movement.
